title: Quantum Theory: Photons, Spectra and Matter Waves
seo_title: Year 12 Physics: Quantum Theory Worksheets (Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Black-body radiation, Wien's law and Planck's quanta; photons and E = hf; the photoelectric effect, work function and threshold frequency; energy levels and line spectra in the Bohr model; de Broglie waves and wave–particle duality. (Senior Secondary Physics, Unit 4: Revolutions in modern physics)
meta_desc: Free Year 12 Physics worksheets on quantum theory: black-body radiation, Wien's law, E = hf, the photoelectric effect, energy levels, line spectra and de Broglie wavelength. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: E = hf = hc/λ; hf = φ + Ek(max).
body_html:
How to think about it

Hot objects emit a black-body spectrum that peaks at λmax = 2.898 × 10⁻³ ÷ T (Wien's law). Planck explained the spectrum by assuming energy comes in quanta; Einstein extended this to photons, E = hf.

In the photoelectric effect one photon frees one electron if hf exceeds the work function φ. Electrons in atoms have fixed energy levels, so atoms emit and absorb photons of particular energies (line spectra). Matter also behaves as waves: λ = h/(mv).

Example

Peak wavelength of a 5800 K star?

λ = 2.898 × 10⁻³ ÷ 5800

Answer: 500 nm

Example

Photon of 3.0 eV on a metal with φ = 2.0 eV. Ek(max)?

3.0 − 2.0

Answer: 1.0 eV

Common mistakes

  • Thinking brighter light gives faster photoelectrons.
  • Forgetting to convert eV to joules (× 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹).
  • Thinking only light can show wave behaviour.
